title: OOM triggered, suspect ARC to blame
body: Our roughly 3 GB buildserver images began suffering OOM kills and failed builds after we integrated the ZFS change from pull request 14359. On one affected EC2 system, only about 7 MB was available even though no userspace process accounted for most of the memory and nearly all 8 GB of swap remained free. arcstat showed an ARC size around 2.7 GB while its target c was about 99 MB and available memory was negative; arcstats similarly showed size around 2.9 GB, mostly MRU data. The OOM killer was terminating userspace processes such as telegraf. I expected the ARC to evict data under this pressure, but it was not doing so.

symptoms_visible: My approximately 3 GB buildserver runs out of available memory and the OOM killer terminates userspace processes during builds, even though most swap is free and process RSS does not account for the missing memory.
At the affected point, arcstat reports roughly 2.7–2.9 GB in the ARC while c is around 99–100 MB and available memory is negative.
N0.label: N0 buildserver OOM with oversized ARC

symptoms_visible: The OOM condition recurs with the ARC around 2.9 GB, c at its minimum near 100 MB, and roughly 2.7 GB reported as MRU data.
N1.label: N1 full ARC counters collected

symptoms_visible: After I started the drop-caches experiment, both CPUs remained busy and the ARC stayed large for about six hours before its size finally fell to roughly 460 MB and available memory rose to about 1.9 GB.
While the ARC was still high, my probe printed arc_is_overflowing return value 2; after the ARC fell, it printed 0.
During the high-memory interval, c collapsed while ARC size and data remained high, and the evict_skip and evict_not_enough counters climbed.
N2.label: N2 delayed ARC eviction observed

symptoms_visible: With the candidate change applied, I ran about 30 builds and none failed with an OOM.
N3.label: N3 candidate correction survives repeated builds

symptoms_visible: After pulling the merged change into our buildserver images, we have not seen the OOM failures recur.
N_terminal.label: terminal buildserver images verified

question_patterns: Can you provide the complete /proc/spl/kstat/zfs/arcstats output from an affected system?
Could you capture full ARC kstats or arc_summary output while the system is in this state?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I lost access to the first system when the build timed out, but I saved the full arcstats output. It has c=104282624, c_min=104282624, size=2914759656, data_size=2713842688, mru_data=2708664832, and mru_evictable_data=2708664832. It also shows evict_skip=4147591, evict_not_enough=386821, and memory_direct_count=14008.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The full counters show the ARC already near c_min with almost no MRU data and most memory instead accounted to a large userspace process.
The exact values vary slightly between reproductions, but size remains around 2.9 GB, c remains around 100 MB, and most of the ARC is reported as evictable MRU data.

question_patterns: Have you overridden zfs_arc_max on these buildserver images?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have not set a numeric arc_max override. `cat /sys/module/zfs/parameters/zfs_arc_max` prints `0`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I explicitly configured zfs_arc_max to consume nearly all physical RAM.

edges.comment: Thread c0-c7, reporter's affected buildserver only: maintainers requested full ARC statistics and checked whether arc_max had been increased. The reporter supplied raw kstat values and the configured parameter value.

question_patterns: On a reproduced system, can you set the corrected shrinker test value, run `echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches`, and record what happens to ARC size over time?
Could you run the drop-caches experiment during the failure and collect ARC and CPU graphs before and after?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it and started the drop-caches experiment. The ARC did not immediately fall; it remained high while both CPUs were busy. About six hours later it finally dropped to roughly 460 MB, c was about 506 MB, and available memory was about 1.9 GB. I attached the memory, CPU, per-CPU, ARC-size, c-versus-size, and eviction-counter graphs from that same system and interval.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The ARC immediately shrank to its minimum as soon as I ran drop_caches, without sustained CPU use or a delay.
The ARC eventually fell after five hours rather than six, with the same prolonged high size and busy CPUs.

question_patterns: Can you probe arc_is_overflowing while the ARC is stuck and again after it shrinks, and paste the raw return values?
What does an arc_is_overflowing return probe print before and after the delayed eviction?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: While I was inspecting the system before the ARC fell, my bpftrace kretprobe repeatedly printed `returned: 2`. After the ARC had evicted, the same probe repeatedly printed `returned: 0`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The probe prints 0 throughout the high-ARC interval as well as after eviction.

edges.comment: Thread c11-c23, reporter's reproduced buildserver: after correcting the earlier tunable typo to zfs_arc_shrinker_limit, the reporter ran the handler-initiated drop-caches measurement and supplied raw timing, counters, probe output, and six graphs. The observation that evict_skip and evict_not_enough rose was volunteered from the same run; the cause remained engineer-side.

question_patterns: Could you apply the patch from #14692 to a test buildserver image, run a series of builds, and report whether the OOM returns?
Please test the provided patch by running the same builds that previously triggered the problem and tell me what happens.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I got #14692 applied and ran about 30 builds with it. None of those builds failed, and I did not see the OOM during that test.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the candidate patch applied, the same ARC growth and OOM returned within three or four builds.
I completed 25 builds rather than 30, with no OOM failures.

edges.comment: Thread c19 and c27-c31, reporter's test image: a maintainer requested testing of the candidate patch, and the reporter applied it and ran approximately 30 builds. This is pre-merge candidate-build verification, so it is modeled as a measurement clarification rather than a persistent production-system change.

solution.intent: Correct the ARC eviction signedness error represented by the successfully tested change, deploy a build containing that correction to the affected buildserver images, and verify under the real repeated-build workload before declaring the OOM resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Use the merged #14692 change in the buildserver image rather than relying on cache dropping or ARC policy tunables. After deployment, run the normal build workload and confirm that the ARC no longer remains far above c until userspace is OOM-killed.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied ARC counters, delayed-eviction measurements, rising eviction counters, and the successful candidate-patch workload test. Identifying the accepted root cause as a signedness problem in ARC eviction was the maintainer's interpretation in c30 and the rationale for the merged correction, not a conclusion produced by the reporter's probes.

edges.comment: Thread c30-c33, same reporter and deployment: the maintainer stated that the observed counters fit the signedness problem addressed by the candidate change, then merged it. The reporter subsequently pulled the merged change into the actual buildserver images and reported no further OOMs; that post-merge production verification is terminal-side evidence, not required upstream information.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as a signedness error in ARC eviction behavior that prevented timely reclaim even while ARC size remained far above c under memory pressure.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: c was driven to its minimum, most ARC memory was reported as evictable MRU data, drop_caches took hours to result in eviction, eviction counters rose, and the candidate correction survived about 30 builds.

Must recommend deploying a build containing the ARC eviction signedness correction; drop_caches, zfs_arc_meta_balance changes, shrinker tuning, or increasing memory must not be presented as the permanent fix.
Must ask for verification with the affected repeated-build workload after deploying the corrected buildserver image and must not declare resolution solely from the pre-merge candidate test.
Resolution requires the reporter's terminal confirmation that the merged correction was incorporated into the actual buildserver images without the OOM failures recurring.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical systems engineer familiar with OpenZFS internals, Linux memory accounting, kstats, bpftrace, kernel tunables, Grafana, and building patched ZFS images.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, collaborative, and evidence-driven; pastes raw counters and commands, supplies graphs, questions hypotheses constructively, and can reproduce builds or apply candidate patches when given specific instructions.
